name: Aristobulus
overview: Aristobulus is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament, specifically noted for being greeted by the Apostle Paul in his epistle to the Romans. Beyond this greeting, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other personal notes. His mention highlights the early Christian community's interconnectedness.
namesAndTitles: The name Aristobulus appears once in the New Testament without a given meaning or divine origin. It is simply recorded as a proper name in Romans 16:10.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Aristobulus beyond the greeting Paul extends to his household, indicating a family or household group associated with him.
scriptureSignificance: Aristobulus is significant as a member of the early Christian community to whom Paul sends greetings, demonstrating the Apostle's pastoral care and the unity among believers. His household's inclusion in Paul's letter reflects the importance of familial and communal bonds within the church. Though details are sparse, his mention affirms the reality of Christian households contributing to the faith's spread.
